title: 6 days Body parts split program review
summary: NH reviews a 6-day machine-heavy body part split from an 18-year-old, 187 cm, skinny French novice. He judges it unsalvageable: too much high-rep machine fluff, no heavy compounds, wrong frequency, and rebuilds a simpler compound-based week.
claims: Fat-loss and bulk cycles should be as long as possible with as small a caloric difference as possible, or you get stuck yo-yoing and waste muscle or gain too much fat
Judge a body part split first by its skeleton: if the named body parts lack synergy the template forces lifts that don't belong together and the frequency will be wrong
A pure 'chest day' doesn't exist: pressing always involves shoulders and triceps, and flyes recruit biceps
Back day always involves forearms and biceps, and lower back work involves glutes and hamstrings, so back and biceps fits naturally
Shoulders plus chest is a good pairing since you cannot press for shoulders without working chest and triceps
Biceps and triceps together isn't synergistic outside an arm day, but a biceps movement on heavy pressing days helps balance and prevent injury
High-mobility joints like the shoulder must be trained with light weight in end ranges; heavy load there causes injury
Pullovers involve a lot of shoulder flexion; keep them in high rep ranges, never near 3RM, or risk chest, triceps, lat or shoulder injury
Weighted shrugs are the best way to grow the traps
A back day of only machines and light dumbbells mimics enhanced pros and is no good for naturals; start with pulls from the floor, rack pulls or block pulls
Machines shouldn't be used for low reps: mechanical failure ruins targeting, it's impractical and dangerous
Avoiding compounds because you wasted time on machines is a sunk cost fallacy; the best time to start deadlifting is now
Even starting with a 135 lb deadlift you can reach 315 in a year
Tall skinny lifters will never gain mass on machines alone; at 6'2 your strength potential is immense and must be built
Those who skip getting strong end up at 25 still skinny blaming genetics
Open chest day with a dumbbell bench at 4x4-8 and gradually move to 3-6 reps or evolving rep ranges instead of everything at 10-12
On chest day prefer a pure vertical press over a second incline press since chest already gets plenty of work
Skull crushers stay in, because the long head of the triceps needs love
Opening a workout with calves is a waste of energy; on leg day start with squats
Leg curls and leg extensions are finishers, not mass builders; you need a squat-type knee flexion, or leg press if you dislike squats
Don't train calves heavy: heavy loads stress the Achilles, feet and ankles and lead to compensating with structure; use light weight, high reps and mind-muscle connection
Isolations call for perfect form and mind-muscle connection, so keep them in high rep ranges
Machines isolate upper back well but always doing the same movements can overwork certain parts
The viewer's lateral raise rep range (likely 4x12) is great; don't go lower in reps on laterals
Lots of rear delt isolation keeps the shoulders healthy
Novices don't need a dedicated arm day; that time should go to compounds or rest
Six training days is pushing it for a novice; most novices can train 3 days a week and progress well
Body part splits are for advanced lifters with high work capacity and recovery, not novices
Done properly a body part split promotes more frequency than PPL or full body; the once-a-week bro split is the bad version
Incline dumbbell curls have too much range, don't protect the biceps tendons and use too much elastic energy; do standing curls for strength at 3-7 reps strict
Even an arm day must respect volume and intensity principles, not 50 sets of fluff
Squatting once a week is not enough frequency
Pyramiding up to 8 reps is essentially a warm-up and leaves you without high-intensity work
Doing abs every day except Sunday is how he got his abs and he still does it
A weakness in mid/lower traps comes from not training them; train them before thinking about nucleus overload
Too much volume in irrelevant intensity windows with irrelevant lifts means minimal progress in three years
French gym culture is obsessed with machines, deadlifting gets you stared at, and the people who get big that way are usually on steroids
With too many machine sets you can never track progression

Rebuilt week: Mon deadlift, machine row, pull-ups, triceps/rear delt superset; Tue horizontal then vertical press; Wed squat, calves, light hinge; Thu vertical press and delt work; Fri rest or arms/upper back/GPP; Sat heavy deadlift and knee-flexion variation
Weighted carries like farmer's walks fit an arms/GPP day because everything is warmed up
Training traps via deadlifts, carries and a dedicated finisher across the week will make them grow
At 18 he weighed the same as this 160 lb viewer
